frequency_question: How often do highly contentious, party-line voting bills pass both chambers (or specifically the Senate) within a designated legislative window once advanced?
membership_rule: Federal bills aimed at altering voter registration, identification, or eligibility requirements that advanced past initial committee stages or received chamber floor votes between 1995 and 2026.

cases.name: SAVE Act House passage / Senate pending 2024

coverage_note: 6 major legislative pushes named; represents the universe of highly polarized federal election administration bills in recent decades.
known_gaps: Excludes minor provisions rider-attached to omnibus appropriations bills.
skeleton: Legislative push cycles for major federal election law over three decades divided into bipartisan consensus windows vs. highly polarized partisan single-party initiatives.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 6 major polarized partisan attempts in divided or narrowly held Congresses
validity_reason: Remains valid through the current congressional cycle until structural Senate rules (such as the filibuster) or major partisan realignments shift.
